issue_context.title: BUG: TypeError: bad operand type for unary -: 'FloatingArray'
issue_context.body:
- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of pandas.

- [ ] (optional) I have confirmed this bug exists on the master branch of pandas.

---

**Note**: Please read [this guide](https://matthewrocklin.com/blog/work/2018/02/28/minimal-bug-reports) detailing how to provide the necessary information for us to reproduce your bug.

#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example

```python
import pandas as pd
x = pd.Series([1, 2, 3], dtype=pd.Float32Dtype())
-x
```

#### Problem description

Should it generate an error? 

`TypeError: bad operand type for unary -: 'FloatingArray'`

#### Expected Output

```python
-1 * x
# like -pd.Series([1, 2, 3])
```

comments: Also: I use ctrl+f in the [patch notes](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/whatsnew/v1.2.0.html) and search for `convert_dtypes` - there is nothing new. Yet, [in API docs we see](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/reference/api/pandas.DataFrame.convert_dtypes.html?highlight=convert_dtypes): *Changed in version 1.2: Starting with pandas 1.2, this method also converts float columns to the nullable floating extension type.*
@hbaniecki thanks for the report. This was fixed for Integer dtype (https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/36303), but should clearly also fix it for Float dtype

Hi all,
I faced with a similar issue when trying to perform an elementary operation with Float data type array:
```
df = pd.DataFrame([1.1,2.1,3.1,4.1], columns=['x'])
df = df.convert_dtypes()
df['x1'] = -df.x
```
I got: 

> TypeError: bad operand type for unary -: 'FloatingArray'

for pandas v 1.2.1 and python v 3.7.9
I'll have a look at this one.
